findings.title: Clearing skills at a switch comes one render too late: the outgoing agent's list is still remembered under the new agent
findings.body: The reset at lines 235-237 runs in an effect, so `setSkills([])` only takes effect on the next render. The remembering effect in `ChatSessionScreen.tsx:380-382` depends on `[conversation.skills, ..., skillsHarness]`. `skillsHarness` comes from `conversation.snapshot?.harness` (line 379), which changes in the same render that reveals the switch. In that commit the effect runs with the outgoing agent's `conversation.skills` and the new `skillsHarness`. It calls `rememberChatSkills(host, newHarness, projectId, oldSkills)`, which stores the old agent's list under the new agent's key. The following render has `skills = []`, and `rememberChatSkills` ignores empty lists (`rememberedSkills.ts:25`), so nothing overwrites it. The New task page then offers the outgoing agent's skills for the new agent, until a later `loadSkills` for the new agent replaces them. That is the problem this PR's comment at line 235 says it fixes. The new test only checks `conversation.skills` and never goes through `ChatSessionScreen` or `rememberedChatSkills`, so it misses this. Fix: pair the skills with the harness they were read for (e.g. `{ harness, list }` state), and have the screen remember only when that harness equals `skillsHarness`. Add a test that asserts `rememberedChatSkills(host, newHarness)` is empty after a switch.

findings.title: Stale-load branch deletes the cache entry that may now belong to the new agent
findings.body: When the stale check at line 400 fires, `skillsCache.delete(cacheKey)` drops whatever entry sits under the key. The switch effect (line 236) already deleted the outgoing agent's entry. By the time the old request resolves, a `loadSkills` for the new agent may have created a pending or cached entry under the same key. The delete removes that entry too, so the next `/` open fetches again. This is harmless but redundant. `asyncValueCache.ts:66` already stops a superseded request from writing its result back, so the delete could go.
